To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the daughters of high milk EPD sires produce more milk and wean heavier calves than those from low-milk EPDs, and that the correlations between milk EPD of sires and total milk production of their daughters and calf performance were moderate.
milk EPD of Hereford and Angus sires are highly correlated with milk production and preweaning growth of crossbred daughters.

milk production of Angus and Herefords was accurately predicted by their sire's milk EPD and that the crossbred daughters of the high-milk EPDs had better calf performance and body condition than did daughters of low-milk sires.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of milk production EPD to improve preweaning calf performance in beef cattle.
the use of milk yield EPDs in the Angus and Hereford breeds.
the genetic and environmental effects on the milk production and preweaning calf performance of crossbred Angus- and Herefordsired dairy beef cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
milk EPD of sires are useful predictors of milk yield of crossbred daughters.
milk EPD are a useful tool in genetic improvement of milk production in beef cows.
the milk production of Angus- and Herefordsired cows and the subsequent performance of their calves are predictable from the milk EPD of the sires.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the milk EPD of sires are sufficiently associated with preweaning performance to be useful in genetic improvement of the preweaning performance in beef cows.
Angus sires with high milk EPD produce more milk, and their crossbred daughters produce more milk and wean heavier calves, than do Angus sires with low milk EPD.
the Angus and Hereford milk EPD are useful tools for genetic improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of milk EPDs can improve the genetic merit of the Angus breed for milk production, which is a trait of economic importance in beef cattle.
milk EPD of the Angus and Hereford breeds are sufficiently associated with the traits of interest that they can be used in selection programs to increase preweaning performance.
the Angus breed has a much greater potential to produce more milk than previously recognized and this milk is associated with greater weaning weights of the calves.
